name: 74LVC2T45DC,125
title: 74LVC2T45 and 74LVCH2T45: dual-supply 2-bit translating transceiver, 3-state
summary: A two-channel logic level translator with two independent supplies, each 1.2 V to 5.5 V. Port A and the DIR pin follow VCC(A), port B follows VCC(B), and DIR picks the direction for both channels. With either supply at ground both ports turn off, and IOFF turns the outputs off on an unpowered part so no damaging current flows back through it. The 74LVCH2T45 adds bus hold on the data inputs. 74LVC2T45DC,125 is the version without bus hold in VSSOP8.
key_figures: 420 Mbps (3.3 V to 5.0 V); 210 Mbps to 3.3 V; 140 Mbps to 2.5 V; 75 Mbps to 1.8 V; 60 Mbps to 1.5 V

notes: Pin 1 is marked at the lower left corner of the package, under the marking code.
No 74LVCH2T45 is offered in SOT1089.

circuits.title: Unidirectional level shifting
circuits.description: Two signals pass from a system on supply VCC2 to a system on supply VCC1. VCC1 feeds VCC(A) and VCC2 feeds VCC(B); DIR is tied to ground, so the B pins are inputs, switching at thresholds set by VCC2, and the A pins drive the system-1 receivers at VCC1 levels. Each supply may be anywhere from 1.2 V to 5.5 V.
notes: Pin roles: VCC(A) = VCC1 (supply of system-1, 1.2 V to 5.5 V); 1A, 2A outputs at VCC1 levels; GND device ground; DIR at GND (LOW) sets B to A; 2B, 1B inputs with thresholds set by VCC2; VCC(B) = VCC2 (supply of system-2, 1.2 V to 5.5 V).

circuits.title: Bidirectional level shifting
circuits.description: One line, 2A to 2B, carries data both ways between system-1 on VCC1 and system-2 on VCC2. System-1 sets the direction through DIR. Channel 1 is unused, with 1A and 1B tied to ground. A pull-up or pull-down holds each side of the line while both ports are off during a turnaround; it is fitted only with the 74LVC2T45, as the 74LVCH2T45 holds the line with its bus hold. The part has no output enable, so the two systems must avoid driving the line against each other when the direction changes.

parts.value: I/O-1, system-1 transceiver with direction control

notes: Each pull-up or pull-down has one end on its line; its other end goes to that side's supply or to ground.

circuits.title: Switching-time test circuit
circuits.description: A pulse generator, terminated by RT, drives the input of the device under test. The output is loaded with CL to ground, RL to ground and a second RL to VEXT. VEXT is open for tPLH and tPHL, at GND for tPZH and tPHZ, and at 2VCCO for tPZL and tPLZ. Input and output are observed at VI and VO.

operation.text: Two non-inverting buffers that carry logic between two supply domains in either direction. Port A (1A, 2A) and the DIR input run from VCC(A); port B (1B, 2B) runs from VCC(B). DIR HIGH sends A to B; DIR LOW sends B to A. One DIR sets both channels.

Each supply may be set anywhere from 1.2 V to 5.5 V, independently, so the part moves signals between any pair of the 1.2 V, 1.5 V, 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V and 5.0 V levels. Inputs accept voltages up to 5.5 V.

If either supply is at GND, both ports go to the high-impedance OFF-state. IOFF circuitry turns the outputs off when the part is unpowered, so no harmful current flows back through it; IOFF is specified for partial power-down use.
The 74LVCH2T45 has active bus-hold circuits that keep an unused or floating data input at its last valid level. The 74LVC2T45 has none.
The input stage of each data I/O is on in every state, including when that pin is acting as an output.
Outputs source and sink ±24 mA with the output supply at 3.0 V. Supply current is 16 µA maximum.

There is no output enable pin, so both systems must avoid driving the line at the same time while the direction changes. The enable times are the longest delay from a DIR change until an output is valid. After a change from A-to-B to B-to-A, port B is disabled first; a signal then applied to B appears at A one propagation delay later.
No supply sequence is needed beyond connecting GND first.
